text.p: The following are leading domestic stories in Portuguese newspapers.
- The Portuguese 1997 budget is not excessively optimistic in terms of revenue forecasts and keeps tight control of spending, Under-Secretary for the Budget Manuela Arcanjo told the paper.

- Portuguese Social Democrat leader Marcelo Rebelo de Sousa told the paper he believes it is lamentable that the government presented its 1997 budget without saying whether or not it would present a supplementary budget for 1996.

- Beer company Unicer is interested in launching a public offer to buy (OPA) for mineral water company Vidago after retailer Jeronimo Martins said it would launch a bid, sources close to Unicer told the paper.
- Portuguese airline TAP will maintain some Air France planes from next year, a TAP official told the paper.
- Jeronimo Martins could sell the hotels of mineral water firm Vidago if it succeeds in its bid, a senior official with the retailer told the paper.
- The Portuguese foreign ministry denied a report that it could have sent arms illegally to eastern Zaire in May 1994 to support exiled Hutus in the civil war in Rwanda.
- The Portuguese government will ask the European Commission to permit the total liberalisation of Portuguese telecommunications from January 1 2000.
- Portuguese bishops will discuss a referendum on abortion at a conference at Fatima in central Portugal, which began yesterday.
- Social Security Minister Eduardo Ferro Rodrigues yesterday announced real pension increases for most pensioners in 1997. The new pensions take effect from December 1.

- Jeronimo Martins is likely to launch its bid for Vidago next year due to the formalities that have to be completed before the formal bid is made. Jeronimo Martins would be interested in selling some of Vidago's real estate.
